This site was built with coding agents, working from a brief and a run of
corrections.
This page is what I asked for and what I said back.
The [JuliaCon 2026 site](https://samabbott.co.uk/JuliaCon2026/prompts.html)
did the same, and the [how I LLM](https://samabbott.co.uk/how-I-llm) deck
before it put its prompt on a slide.

## The brief

This is my opening prompt, rewritten as plain prose and grouped under
headings.
The spelling and grammar are corrected and the sentences are complete.
The judgements are unchanged and nothing has been added.
The verbatim version, typos and all, is
[in the repo][orig].
It began with the workshop programme and the organisers' request, which are
on the talk pages.

[orig]: https://github.com/seabbs/AIandIDVUB/blob/main/notes/original-brief.md

### The site

::: {.prompt}
I am not yet sure what to put in these talks.
To begin, use agents to create a folder in seabbs called AIandIDVUB, with
the same structure as the one I made for JuliaCon 2026.
Put the slide decks in place with their titles and QR codes, but leave the
content for now.
I will then make a matching GitHub repository and give you access to push
to it.
I think the abstract for each talk can be the organisers' request, as
bullets.
:::

### The research

::: {.prompt}
Use agents to search my recent work for anything related.
I am unsure whether the organisers mean agentic AI, deep learning,
universal differential equations, or something else.
:::

### The keynote

::: {.prompt}
Before I looked back at what the workshop covers, I had planned the first
talk in a few sections.
The first would be a ten minute introduction to outbreak modelling over the
ten years or so I have been in the field.
It would cover Ebola in West Africa, which I was aware of and others worked
on, then COVID-19, mpox and the current Ebola outbreak.
The second would be ten minutes on agentic AI.
I have material on this from how I LLM, but I also want to ask what it
means for modelling.
The third might be ten minutes on the opportunities in other AI models.
Universal differential equations, physics-informed neural networks and
neural flows for fitting, on which the nfidd course had a little, at a high
level.
Perhaps foundation models for outbreaks and infectious disease forecasting,
spun out of the current time series foundation models.
Perhaps agentic model composition, such as Google's forecasting success at
FluSight.
:::

### The communication lecture

::: {.prompt}
For the communication lecture I am not sure what to do.
Mine my recent work and give me a proposal.
:::

### How it should look

::: {.prompt}
Look at the git history of my recent talks to see how I have pruned and
refined the language and style to make them my own, and follow that.
Be wary of dense text on slides.
We like schematics, pictures and sparse, clean slides.
:::

## How it was built

Five research agents ran first, before any slide was written, and wrote
their notes into
[`notes/`](https://github.com/seabbs/AIandIDVUB/tree/main/notes).

- what I have already said about coding agents, and the live DRC outbreak
  model built with them
- what my teaching and grants say about the other AI methods, and what the
  literature says about foundation models, universal differential
  equations, and flows in epidemiology
- my record of communicating with government, the public, and other
  scientists during COVID-19
- what the other speakers work on, and so what this workshop means by AI
- a timeline of the outbreaks I have worked on or watched

The style notes were carried over from the JuliaCon 2026 build, including
the catalogue of LLM phrasing I strip out of my own slides.
The prompts on this page and the abstracts on the talk pages were rewritten
by an agent, on the steer above.
The [commit history](https://github.com/seabbs/AIandIDVUB/commits/main) is
the record of what happened next.
